Retro nonsense, correctly applied

CV in a Box

A CV packaged like old software. Completely unnecessary, took far longer than writing a CV. I wanted to know whether something people pick up beats something people skim.

Watch the design video Open front artwork PDF
BUILD SPEC RUN OF ONE
Box format
Big-box PC game, the size software used to come in. Underneath it is a cereal box with printed panels glued on, then shrink-wrapped.
Artwork
Drawn in Inkscape, modelled on an old Windows 95 box. Open source tools for a box pretending to be shrink-wrapped commercial software.
Print process
Photo paper on a refillable-tank Canon inkjet, which is both cheaper and better than cartridges. Colours came out right first time.
Contents
The printed CV. Plus a fake serial number and a fake hologram seal, because a box that does not pretend to be worried about piracy is not a real box.
Print run
One.
Cost per box
Pennies, plus registered postage and a lost evening.

Did it work

The one box went to one company, registered post, and I never heard back. So: no. As an object it works exactly as intended — it sits on a shelf between real software boxes and people pick it up to find out what it is, which was the whole hypothesis. Whether anyone at the other end took it out of the envelope, I have no idea.

What I would change

It was a one-off and I am not sure I would repeat it. If I did, I would send more than one, and I would aim it at somewhere more likely to open the box.

Build video

The design video

Short video of the design work. Premise is silly, execution deliberately is not.

Why

Because a PDF is obedient.

A normal CV lists what you did. This one shows I will take a daft idea all the way through artwork, print and assembly before admitting it was a lot of work for a joke.

What it says

Memorable beats compliant

A small protest against every application looking the same. The back lists the real things - software engineering, Linux, Python - as a 1990s feature list.

Does it work

The shelf test

Sits on a shelf between actual software boxes. People pick it up to see what it is. That was the only thing I wanted.
